title: Red Team Handoff + Triage Check-in (2026-05-04)
content:
Meeting: Red Team Handoff + Triage Check-in
Date: 2026-05-04 10:00-10:45 PT
Attendees: Priya (owner), Evan, Lucas, Maya, Samira, + ad-hoc from Platform (J. Ortiz)
Purpose: quick handoff from red-team run, prioritize vuln backlog items, align on secrets scanning tuning, and schedule threat-modeling spike for Private/KMS flow.

Summary (top lines)
- Red-team run (2026-05-02) surfaced 6 findings: 2 medium-risk (auth cookie leakage + tmp S3 ACL), 3 low-risk misconfigurations, 1 informational (logging detail).
- We performed an initial triage during the meeting; owners assigned and fast-fix plan agreed for the two medium items.
- Secrets scanner noise continues for terraform state outputs; agreed next steps to reduce FP rate by 60% via regex tuning + allowlist.
- Threat-modeling spike to be scheduled for week of 2026-05-11 focused on Private deployment: KMS integration, key rotation, and ephemeral node onboarding.

Raw notes from discussion
- Red-team findings:
  - R1 (MED): session cookie transmitted in some internal worker logs (red-team found via replay). Repro steps and PoC in PR #482. Impact: user session theft on low-latency internal networks.
  - R2 (MED): temp S3 bucket created during integration test had ACL that leaked object list to internal-corp account. Impact: medium (no public read, but wider org access).
  - R3-R5 (LOW): deprecated TLS cipher negotiation on legacy infra; outdated dependency (libyaml2) with non-exploitable CVE; admin console shows extra debug endpoint behind feature flag.
  - R6 (INFO): verbose SQL errors in staging logs (no PII).

- Triage rubric used (quick score):
  - Exploitability: 0-3 (3 = trivial remote), Exposure: 0-3 (3 = public prod), Impact: 0-4 (data exfil, RTO), Confidence: 0-2 (PoC quality).
  - R1 = Exploitability 2, Exposure 1, Impact 3, Confidence 2 => score 8 => MED.
  - R2 = 2,2,2,1 => 7 => MED.

Decisions & immediate actions
- Fast patch for R1 (session cookie in logs):
  - Action: remove cookie from worker logs + add sanitizer in logging lib.
  - Owner: Lucas Chen.
  - Due: 2026-05-06 (code PR + canary deploy).
  - Linked: github.com/redwood-inference/worker-logging/commit/7a3b (see PR #486).

- R2 (temp S3 ACL):
  - Action: revoke ACL, add CI gate to check bucket ACLs for non-prod infra, and migrate test fixture to internal-mock S3.
  - Owner: Maya Rodriguez (infra eng).
  - Due: 2026-05-08 for revocation, 2026-05-18 for CI gate.
  - Linked: JIRA-SEC-2213 (S3 ACL remediation).

- Low / informational items:
  - Legacy TLS negotiation: schedule a patch wave to disable ciphers in the 2026-05-25 maintenance window. Owner: Platform Eng (J. Ortiz).
  - Debug endpoint behind flag: confirm no prod exposure; if safe, remove endpoint in next sprint. Owner: Samira Ahmed.

Secrets scanning (ongoing pain)
- Problem: scanner yields ~45% false positives from terraform state outputs and internal test keys. Noise is drowning high-fidelity findings.
- Quick wins agreed now:
  - Add allowlist for terraform state object patterns (owner: Evan Park, due 2026-05-07).
  - Implement context-aware scoring in scanner: reduce severity for matches that are inside known test fixture paths (owner: Priya Shah + security infra, due 2026-05-14).
  - Run a one-off manual sweep of the last 100 scanner alerts to produce an FP taxonomy (task assigned to Evan + Lucas, due 2026-05-10).
- Longer term: integrate secret-detection into CI pipeline with enriched analyzers (SAST + entropy checks) (epic: JIRA-SEC-2240).

Threat-modeling spike: Private deployments (KMS flow)
- Motivation: Private mode introduces customer KMS and local key wrapping. Need to validate key usage lifecycle (rotation, wrap/unwrap), threat surface of ephemeral worker nodes, and policy enforcement in control plane.
- Spike goals (2-day):
  - Map dataflow for model keys: where plaintext keys appear, when an unwrap happens, and persistence windows.
  - Simulate key-rotation scenarios and observe failover behavior (canary vs mass rotation).
  - Produce a proposed set of mitigations: TLS pinning between control plane and customer KMS, HSM-backed caching, and audit hooks.
- Proposed owners: Priya (lead), Samira (architect), Platform Eng support (J. Ortiz).
- Schedule: May 11-12. Deliverable: Confluence draft + risk matrix (confluence:SEC-THREAT-2026-04 updated).

Playbook updates & runbook notes
- Add an "S3 temporary artifact review" checklist to incident playbook (small PR in repo after R2 is closed). Owner: Maya.
- Add logging sanitizer checks to pre-merge checklist for services that write session-level metadata. Owner: Lucas.
- Escalation matrix tweaked: medium findings with evidence get 24-48h fix window; if fix misses window, escalate to Eng Director + CISO on-call.

Backlog grooming (quick pass)
- High-priority items to add to next sprint planning:
  - Improve secret-scanner precision (epic: SEC-2240).
  - Logging sanitizer SDK rollout to 6 services.
  - CI ACL gate for S3 + enforcement job.
- Lower-priority: TLS cipher cleanup (maintenance window), remove debug endpoints, dependency update for libyaml2.

Open questions / unresolved items
- How to handle customers who require long-lived test keys for on-prem staging? (Ops input needed)
- Can Platform schedule config-management change for S3 ACL enforcement before May 18? (J. Ortiz check)
- Clarify canonical owner for secret-scanner rulebook (tooling vs sec-eng). Proposal: sec-eng will own rules; tooling will maintain runner.

Action items (recap)
- Lucas: PR sanitizer + canary (due 2026-05-06).
- Maya: revoke ACL + add S3 CI gate plan (revocation due 2026-05-08).
- Evan: allowlist and FP taxonomy sweep (allowlist due 2026-05-07, taxonomy due 2026-05-10).
- Priya + Samira: threat-modeling spike deliverable (confluence draft due 2026-05-13).
- Team: add playbook checklist PRs once fixes land (owners above).

Quick log (standup-style)
- 10:02 Lucas: confirmed logging lib change minimal and low-risk to roll.
- 10:10 Maya: found automation to mass-revoke ACLs; will test in staging.
- 10:18 Evan: scanner allowlist prototype ready locally; will push to staging ruleset.
- 10:30 Priya: set spike schedule; asked Platform for a 2-hr slot for KMS test harness.

Notes-to-self / followups
- Attach PoCs to JIRA items and mark R1/R2 as "in remediation".
- Update confluence:SEC-THREAT-2026-04 with spike plan and expected artifacts.
- Add a short blurb to next all-hands (ops->engineering) about the red-team run and the two medium items being addressed.

Next meeting
- Quick check-in 2026-05-11 09:30 PT to confirm R1 rollback/canary success and scanner allowlist deployment. Full triage sync on 2026-05-18 to review completed CI gates and final playbook updates.

---
Document tone: working notes. Rough sections, TODOs, and links to artifacts included.
